### Figure 1A

-   A: Explained variance after MOFA

```{r}
# Metadata on cell line names
cell_line_metadata <- read_csv(here("data/cell_line_metadata.csv"))
dim(cell_line_metadata)
head(cell_line_metadata)

# Load data for integration
omics_datasets <- list(
  "amines" = read_csv(here(data_dir, "amines.csv")) |>
    column_to_rownames("amine_metabolite"),
  "polar metabolomics" = read_csv(here(data_dir, "polar.csv")) |>
    column_to_rownames("polar_metabolite"),
  "metabolite rates" = read_csv(here(data_dir, "metabolite_rates.csv")) |>
    column_to_rownames("metabolite"),
  "lipid classes" = read_csv(here(data_dir, "lipids.csv")) |>
    column_to_rownames("lipid_metabolite"),
  "pathways" = read_csv(here(data_dir, "pathway_scores.csv")) |>
    column_to_rownames("pathway")
)
# Keep cell lines measured in all datasets.
(common_cell_lines <- lapply(omics_datasets, colnames) |>
  reduce(intersect))
cell_line_metadata <- cell_line_metadata |>
  filter(cell_line %in% common_cell_lines)

lapply(omics_datasets, dim)
omics_datasets <- lapply(
  omics_datasets,
  function(df) select(df, all_of(common_cell_lines))
)
lapply(omics_datasets, dim)

# Convert to matrix for MOFA2
omics_datasets <- lapply(omics_datasets, as.matrix)
names(omics_datasets)

# Prepare MOFA
MOFA_object <- create_mofa(omics_datasets)
print(MOFA_object)
plot_data_overview(MOFA_object)

# Define options
data_opts <- get_default_data_options(MOFA_object)
head(data_opts)
model_opts <- get_default_model_options(MOFA_object)
model_opts$num_factors <- 8
head(model_opts)
train_opts <- get_default_training_options(MOFA_object)
head(train_opts)
```


```{r}
#| eval: false

if (rerun_mofa) {
# Build MOFA Object
MOFA_object <- prepare_mofa(
  object = MOFA_object,
  data_options = data_opts,
  model_options = model_opts,
  training_options = train_opts
)

# Run MOFA
model_file <- here(output_dir, "Figure1A_MOFA_model.hdf5")
reticulate::use_condaenv("mofa_env")
MOFA_object_trained <- run_mofa(MOFA_object, model_file)
}
```

Alternatively, when the model has been built already: load the model and put a copy
in the output directory

```{r}
if (!rerun_mofa) {
MOFA_object_trained <- load_model(model_file)
file.copy(model_file, here(output_dir, "Figure1A_MOFA_model_copy.hdf5"))
}
```

After peer review comments: define a clear cutoff for factors to keep. 
This will be at least 1% variation in at least 1 dataset.

```{r}
MOFA2::calculate_variance_explained(MOFA_object_trained)
MOFA2::get_variance_explained(MOFA_object_trained)

# AI assisted code. AI-generated with GPT-5.6 Luna, 2026-10-08: filter MOFA2 factors with >1% R2 in at least two datasets. Debugged by Hanneke
filter_mofa_factors <- function(mofa) {
  r2 <- mofa@cache$variance_explained$r2_per_factor$group1

  keep <- rowSums(r2 > 1) >= 2
  factors <- rownames(r2)[keep]

  mofa_subset <- subset_factors(mofa, factors = factors)

  return(mofa_subset)
}
# End AI-assisted code

MOFA_object_trained <- filter_mofa_factors(MOFA_object_trained)
```


### Figure 1B-C

-   B: correlations with proliferation for factors 1, 2, and 7
-   C: correlations with subtype for factors 1, 2, and 7

And in main text: ANOVA with subtype and factor.

```{r}
factors <- get_factors(MOFA_object_trained, as.data.frame = TRUE) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = factor, values_from = value) |>
  left_join(cell_line_metadata, by = c("sample" = "cell_line")) |>
  rename(cell_line = sample)

dim(factors)
head(factors)
factors |>
  write_csv(here(output_dir, "Figure1BC.csv"))
```

Note that it is not corrected for multiple testing:

```{r}
for (factor in 1:ncol(get_factors(MOFA_object_trained)$group1)) {
  print(str_glue("*****Correlation proliferation for Factor{factor}*****"))
  cor_nr <- cor(
    factors[["ProliferationRate"]],
    factors[[str_glue("Factor{factor}")]],
    method = "spearman", use = "pairwise.complete.obs"
  )
  print(cor_nr)
  result <- lm(
    as.formula(str_glue("Factor{factor} ~ ProliferationRate")),
    data = factors
  )
  print(summary(result))
}
```

```{r}
for (factor in 1:ncol(get_factors(MOFA_object_trained)$group1)) {
  print(str_glue("*****ANOVA for Factor{factor}*****"))
  result <- lm(
    as.formula(str_glue("Factor{factor} ~ Subtype_4_categories")),
    data = factors
  )
  anova_result <- anova(result)
  print(anova_result)
  print(summary(result))
}
```

After peer review: Include statistics related to post hoc comparison. I selected Tukey's Honest Significance Difference for MOFA factors based on code from: Leegwater, H., Zhang, Z., Zhang, X., Wang, X., Hankemeier, T., Zweemer, A. J. M., van de Water, B., Danen, E., Hoekstra, M., Harms, A. C., Kindt, A., & Le Dévédec, S. E. (2025). Distinct lipidomic profiles in breast cancer cell lines relate to proliferation and EMT phenotypes. Biochimica et Biophysica Acta (BBA) - Molecular and Cell Biology of Lipids, 1870(7), 159679. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.bbalip.2025.159679

Calculate Tukey HSD

```{r}

for (factor in 1:ncol(get_factors(MOFA_object_trained)$group1)) {
  print(str_glue("*****ANOVA for Factor{factor}*****"))
  result <- lm(as.formula(str_glue("Factor{factor} ~ Subtype_4_categories")), data = factors)
  anova_result <- anova(result)
  print(anova_result)
  print(summary(result))
  
  significance_levels <-  TukeyHSD(aov(result))
  print(significance_levels)
}
```

### Figure 1F

Show glutamine-glutamate in a different unit.

```{r}
metabolite_rates_unscaled <- read_csv(here(
  data_dir,
  "metabolite_rates_unscaled.csv"
)) |>
  pivot_longer(-metabolite, names_to = "cell_line", values_to = "value") |>
  pivot_wider(
    id_cols = cell_line,
    names_from = metabolite, values_from = value
  ) |>
  select(cell_line, `Glutamine rate`, `Glutamic acid rate`) |>
  # Convert glutamine uptake to a release rate
  mutate(`Glutamine rate` = `Glutamine rate` * -1) |>
  rename(
    `Glutamine uptake (µm/gDw/h)` = `Glutamine rate`,
    `Glutamic acid secretion (µm/gDw/h)` = `Glutamic acid rate`
  )

write_csv(metabolite_rates_unscaled, here(output_dir, "Figure1F.csv"))
```
